title: Nights out on the Grand Strand

p: The Carolina shag is a smooth, easygoing partner dance that grew up along this coast in the 1940s, when college students came to dance to beach music on Ocean Drive. South Carolina made it the official state dance in 1984. It is still danced in North Myrtle Beach every week, and a few clubs there are built around it.

Duck's Beach Club, Fat Harold's and OD Arcade and Lounge are all within walking distance of each other on and around Main Street, and the Spanish Galleon sits at the Horseshoe where Main Street meets Ocean Drive. You do not need to know how to shag to go in. Duck's offers lessons, and the dance floors are friendly to beginners.

The Bowery on 9th Avenue North has been open since 1944 and is known as an early home of the band Alabama in the 1970s. It is still a country bar with live music most nights. Apache Pier and the Pier at Garden City mix live music with an ocean view. Ocean Annie's does the beach-bar thing by the pool, and Dead Dog Saloon is the live music anchor of the MarshWalk in Murrells Inlet, where the sunset over the marsh is part of the show.

At the other end of the scale, 3001 Nightlife puts three clubs under one roof, and Señor Frog's at Broadway at the Beach is a louder party spot. Comedy Cabana is the pick if you would rather laugh than dance.

list: Venues change hands and hours more than most places. Check the venue's own page or social media for tonight's band or event.
Parking near Ocean Drive and Broadway at the Beach fills up on summer nights. A rideshare or a short walk from your hotel is easier.
Alcohol is not allowed on most local beaches, so keep the drinks for the venue.
Many of these places are seasonal, and a few are quiet or closed in winter.
